```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
library(data.table)
library(DT)
# R code here uses HTML entities, not Unicode characters, so the page renders the same in any build
# locale (in a non-UTF-8 R session, a Greek Delta in an R string comes out as <U+0394>)
A <- "docs/assets/gwas_catalog"
ov <- fread(file.path(A, "overview.tsv")); cand <- fread(file.path(A, "candidates.tsv"), colClasses=list(character=c("np_p", "bb_p")))
bh <- fread(file.path(A, "brain_hits.tsv"), colClasses=list(character=c("best_p", "or_beta", "pubmed")))
ck <- fread(file.path(A, "gnl3_checks.tsv"))
parts <- fread(file.path(A, "parts.tsv")); gnotes <- fread(file.path(A, "gene_notes.tsv"), colClasses="character", na.strings=NULL)
steps <- fread(file.path(A, "steps.tsv")); lc <- fread(file.path(A, "lookup_counts.tsv"))
rules <- fread(file.path(A, "trait_rules.tsv")); traits <- fread(file.path(A, "trait_terms.tsv"))
fmt <- function(n) format(n, big.mark=",", trim=TRUE, scientific=FALSE)
ent <- function(x) vapply(x, function(z) if (is.na(z)) z else { cp <- utf8ToInt(enc2utf8(z)); paste(ifelse(cp > 127, sprintf("&#%d;", cp), sapply(cp, intToUtf8)), collapse="") }, "", USE.NAMES=FALSE)
pfmt <- function(p) { x <- as.numeric(p); e <- floor(log10(x)); m <- round(x / 10^e); sprintf("%g &times; 10<sup>%d</sup>", m, e) }
lcv <- function(k) lc[item == k, value]
sv <- function(col, ver="read_based", k=0.05) steps[version == ver & cutoff == k][[col]]   # main cutoff: 0.05
ckv <- function(k) ck[check == k, value]
kw <- function(cl, r) gsub("|", ", ", rules[class == cl & rule == r, terms], fixed=TRUE)
RUN <- c(read_based="Read-based", transcript_based="Transcript-based")
o05 <- ov[version == "read_based" & cutoff == 0.05]
rb <- cand[version == "read_based"]; tb <- cand[version == "transcript_based"]
c1 <- function(g, col, d=rb) d[gene == g][[col]]
hit <- function(trait, p, study) fifelse(is.na(trait) | !nzchar(trait), "",
  sprintf("%s (p = %s; %s)", ent(trait), sapply(p, function(x) if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) "" else pfmt(x)), study))
NOTES <- c(LY6H="our variant is the GWAS lead SNP; LY6H modulates nicotinic receptors",
           GNL3="same splicing event as a published GNL3 sQTL in brain (below)",
           HNRNPK="significant at all three timepoints",
           FLOT1="MHC; reported only without the clustering filter")
cand_table <- function(d) d[brain_hit == TRUE][order(match(gene, names(NOTES)))][, .(Gene=gene, `Variant (rsID)`=rsid,
  Timepoints=tps, `Best q`=signif(q, 2), `&Delta;PSI (reads)`=sprintf("%+.0f pp (%s)", 100 * dpsi, fmt(reads)),
  `Neuropsychiatric disorder`=hit(np_trait, np_p, np_study), `Brain or behaviour`=hit(bb_trait, bb_p, bb_study),
  Note=fifelse(gene %in% names(NOTES), NOTES[gene], ""))]
hits_dt <- function(d) DT::datatable(as.data.frame(d[, .(Gene=gene, Variant=rsid, `Reported as`=reported_snp, `Risk allele`=risk_allele, Class=trait_class,
  Trait=ent(mapped_trait), `Reported trait`=ent(example_trait), p=as.numeric(best_p), `OR or beta`=or_beta, Study=study,
  Accession=sprintf('<a href="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/studies/%s">%s</a>', accession, accession),
  PubMed=sprintf('<a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/%s/">%s</a>', pubmed, pubmed),
  Entries=associations)]), escape=FALSE, rownames=FALSE, extensions="Buttons", width="100%",
  options=list(pageLength=10, scrollX=TRUE, dom="Bfrtip", buttons=c("copy", "csv")))
# the same three items for every gene: its tested parts (0.05 cutoff) with our association and the
# annotation, the variants' GWAS Catalog entries, and the gene annotation
blank <- function(x) { x <- as.character(x); fifelse(is.na(x) | !nzchar(x), "none", x) }
gene_block <- function(g) {
  p <- parts[version == "read_based" & gene == g & nearest_005 == TRUE][order(p_start)]
  a <- gnotes[gene == g]; b <- bh[version == "read_based" & gene == g][order(as.numeric(best_p))]
  dist <- fifelse(p$dist == 0, "inside the part", sprintf("%s bases from the part", fmt(p$dist)))
  part_lines <- sprintf(paste0("- %s:%s-%s (%d bases). Variant %s, %s. Reported at %s; strongest at %s: q = %s, ",
    "&Delta;PSI %+.0f pp, %s reads from %d heterozygous donors. Annotated transcripts: %d of %d %s the part, ",
    "%d %s over it, %d %s not reach it."),
    p$p_chr, fmt(p$p_start), fmt(p$p_end), p$part_len, p$rsid, dist, gsub(",", ", ", p$tps_005), p$tp_best,
    signif(p$min_q, 2), 100 * p$dpsi_best, fmt(p$het_cov_best), p$n_het_best, p$tx_include, p$tx_total,
    fifelse(p$tx_include == 1, "includes", "include"), p$tx_splice_over, fifelse(p$tx_splice_over == 1, "splices", "splice"),
    p$tx_not_reaching, fifelse(p$tx_not_reaching == 1, "does", "do"))
  u <- unique(p[, .(rsid, n_entries)])
  cat_lines <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(u)), function(i) {
    x <- b[rsid == u$rsid[i]]
    br <- if (nrow(x) == 0) "none" else paste(sprintf("%s (p = %s; %s)", ent(x$example_trait),
      sapply(x$best_p, pfmt), x$study), collapse="; ")
    sprintf("- %s: %d %s; brain-related: %s.", u$rsid[i], u$n_entries[i], if (u$n_entries[i] == 1) "entry" else "entries", br)
  }, "")
  cat("**Tested parts and our association**\n\n", paste(part_lines, collapse="\n"), "\n\n",
      "**GWAS Catalog entries of the variants**\n\n", paste(cat_lines, collapse="\n"), "\n\n",
      sprintf("**Gene annotation**: neuronal GO term: %s; autism or developmental disorder: %s; expression after stimulation: %s; splicing after stimulation: %s.\n\n",
              blank(a$neuronal_go), blank(paste(c(a$sfari, a$ddg2p)[nzchar(c(a$sfari, a$ddg2p))], collapse="; ")),
              blank(a$expression_response), blank(a$stimulation_splicing)), sep="")
}
trait_table <- function(cl) knitr::kable(traits[term_class == cl, .(Trait=ent(efo_term),
  `Read-based genes`=genes_read_based, `Transcript-based genes`=genes_transcript_based, `Catalog entries`=associations)])
```

We asked whether the variants behind our allele-specific splicing associations
are known GWAS hits for neuropsychiatric traits. For each variant we read its
entries in the GWAS Catalog, the same list the Catalog shows on its page for the
rsID. A shared hit means the variant affects both splicing and the trait in
different studies. It does not show that the splicing change causes the trait.

**Short answer.** `r o05$genes_either` of the `r o05$genes` genes reported by
read-based isoLASER carry a variant that is itself a genome-wide GWAS hit for a
neuropsychiatric, brain or behaviour trait:

- **LY6H**: smoking initiation (p = 3 × 10<sup>-24</sup>). LY6H modulates
  nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.
- **GNL3**: intelligence. Our association also looks like the same splicing
  event as a published GNL3 splicing QTL in brain.
- **HNRNPK**: a sleep health score.
- **FLOT1**: major depression. It lies in the MHC, so this one is weak.

None of the transcript-based variants is a brain-related hit.

# How the lookup works

1. **Start from our reported associations.** We use the current runs, without
   the clustering filter. An association is one variant × exonic part at one
   timepoint. It is reported when q < 0.05, isoLASER labels it cis and
   \|ΔPSI\| ≥ 0.05. Read-based isoLASER reports `r sv("associations")`
   associations, at `r sv("parts")` exonic parts in `r sv("genes")` genes
   (transcript-based: `r sv("associations", "transcript_based")`,
   `r sv("parts", "transcript_based")` and `r sv("genes", "transcript_based")`).
   The other pages use 0.10; it is shown here for comparison.
2. **Keep one variant per exonic part.** A part often has several reported
   variants on the same haplotype. For each gene × exonic part, we keep the
   reported variant nearest to the part (distance 0 when inside it). This leaves
   `r sv("variants")` of `r sv("variants_all")` read-based variants.
3. **Find each variant's rsID.** We take it from the record in our genotype panel
   with the same position, REF and ALT. Every variant has one.
4. **Look up the variant in the GWAS Catalog.**
   - We use the Catalog release of 2026-10-22: `r fmt(lcv("catalog_associations"))`
     entries for `r fmt(lcv("catalog_snps"))` SNPs.
   - We match entries by the rsID, or by the same GRCh38 position, and both
     always agree here.
   - This gives the same list as the Catalog's page for the rsID. For example,
     rs1108842 (GNL3) has four entries: intelligence and three for adiponectin
     levels.
   - `r sv("variants_matched")` of the `r sv("variants")` read-based variants
     have at least one entry.
5. **Keep genome-wide hits** (p ≤ 5 × 10<sup>-8</sup>). The Catalog also accepts
   entries with p down to 10<sup>-5</sup>, but every entry matched here is
   genome-wide.
6. **Keep neuropsychiatric and brain traits.** Each trait is classed as a
   neuropsychiatric disorder or a brain or behaviour trait. The rules and the
   traits found are under [Trait classes](#trait-classes).
7. **Summarise per gene.** For each gene and class, we show the entry with the
   smallest p.

```{r steps}
lab <- c(associations="1. Reported associations", parts="1. Exonic parts", genes="1. Genes",
         variants="2. Variants (nearest to each part)", variants_matched="4. Variants with a Catalog entry",
         catalog_matches="4. Catalog entries matched", gw_matches="5. Genome-wide (p &le; 5 &times; 10<sup>-8</sup>)",
         gw_np="6. Neuropsychiatric disorder", gw_bb="6. Brain or behaviour")
m <- melt(steps, id.vars=c("version", "cutoff"), measure.vars=names(lab))
m[, col := sprintf("%s, %.2f", RUN[version], cutoff)]
w <- dcast(m, variable ~ col, value.var="value")
w[, Step := lab[as.character(variable)]][, variable := NULL]
setcolorder(w, c("Step", sprintf("%s, %.2f", RUN[c("read_based", "transcript_based")], 0.05), sprintf("%s, %.2f", RUN[c("read_based", "transcript_based")], 0.10)))
knitr::kable(w[, lapply(.SD, function(x) if (is.numeric(x)) fmt(x) else x)])
```

Columns are the run and the \|ΔPSI\| cutoff. The Catalog rows count entries,
and one study can contribute several. The last two rows are subsets of the
genome-wide row. Compared with 0.10, the 0.05 cutoff adds
`r sv("variants") - sv("variants", k=0.10)` read-based variants and one gene
(C11orf58). None of the added variants has a Catalog entry, so the hits are the
same at both cutoffs.

The Catalog records each study's top associations, not full summary statistics.
These are the SNPs at p < 10<sup>-5</sup> that the authors describe as
independent, or the strongest SNP within 100 kb
([inclusion criteria](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/docs/methods/criteria/)). A
study that reported a different SNP for the same signal is therefore not counted
here.

# Overview

```{r overview}
knitr::kable(ov[order(cutoff, version), .(Run=RUN[version], `&Delta;PSI cutoff`=sprintf("%.2f", cutoff), `Exonic parts`=parts, Genes=genes,
                    `Neuropsychiatric disorder`=genes_neuropsych, `Brain or behaviour`=genes_brain_behaviour, Either=genes_either)])
```

**Exonic parts** and **Genes**: reported exonic parts and their genes; each part
contributes its nearest variant. **Neuropsychiatric disorder**, **Brain or
behaviour** and **Either**: genes whose variant has a genome-wide Catalog entry
in that class.

# Read-based isoLASER

`r nrow(rb[brain_hit == TRUE])` of the `r nrow(rb)` read-based genes carry a
variant with a brain-related Catalog entry:

```{r read_based}
knitr::kable(cand_table(rb), escape=FALSE)
```

**Variant (rsID)**: the variant nearest to the
gene's reported parts. **Timepoints**: where the association is reported.
**Best q** and **ΔPSI (reads)**: from the gene's strongest
association. ΔPSI is ALT minus REF inclusion in percentage points; reads are
those from the heterozygous donors. **Neuropsychiatric disorder** and **Brain or
behaviour**: the variant's Catalog entry in that class with the smallest p. All
entries are [listed below](#all-brain-related-hits), with risk alleles and
effects.

The other `r nrow(rb[brain_hit == FALSE])` genes have no brain-related entry: `r paste(rb[brain_hit == FALSE, gene], collapse=", ")`.

Each of the four genes below shows the same items. The tested parts are those
reported, with the 1-based GRCh38 coordinates of each part. The annotation counts use the IsoQuant annotation that isoLASER tests against. The
gene annotation is the same as on the
[main read-based page](isolaser_fdr_reads10nc.html#genes-to-follow-up). A short
note on the event and the gene follows.

## LY6H

```{r block_ly6h, results="asis"}
gene_block("LY6H")
```

**Note.** The two parts are adjacent. The 12-base part is the very start of
LY6H-201's first exon, and the 42-base part follows it. The test compares the
use of two first exons. The [main page](isolaser_fdr_reads10nc.html#ly6h)
shows rs10109061, another of the gene's three reported variants (all within
0.6 kb of each other). LY6H belongs to the Ly6 family of neurotoxin-like proteins
and limits α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor function in neurons
([Puddifoot 2015](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4339353/);
[Moriwaki 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-020-68947-7)). Nicotine
acts on these receptors, so the smoking signal fits the gene's function.

## GNL3

```{r block_gnl3, results="asis"}
gene_block("GNL3")
```

**Note.** The two parts are the stretch between the two annotated ends of exon 1:
52,686,105 in most transcripts and 52,686,202 in ENST00000394799. The test is
therefore about where exon 1 ends (our reading of the annotation). GNL3 lies in
the 3p21.1 schizophrenia and bipolar disorder locus and has been prioritised as a
bipolar risk gene there, from other SNPs
([Molecular Psychiatry](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41380-020-00866-5)). A
schizophrenia study reports that rs2590846 changes "an alternative exonic boundary
in GNL3" in brain
([Science Advances](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.adw7667)).
We read the reported coordinates as hg19, because in hg38 they fall in NEK4; this
is our inference. Moved to hg38, that junction
(`r paste(fmt(as.integer(strsplit(ckv("published junction hg38"), "-")[[1]])), collapse=" to ")`) ends just before exon 2 and
contains both of our parts, so both studies see variants changing where exon 1
ends. We read only the abstract and excerpts of that paper.

## HNRNPK

```{r block_hnrnpk, results="asis"}
gene_block("HNRNPK")
```

**Note.** HNRNPK is the only one of the four genes reported at all three
timepoints. Its two parts carry different nearest variants:

- an 80-base exon that most transcripts include, with rs296888;
- a 34-base stretch present in few transcripts, with rs296887 3 bases away.

Only rs296888 has a brain-related entry. HNRNPK encodes the RNA-binding protein
hnRNP K.

## FLOT1

```{r block_flot1, results="asis"}
gene_block("FLOT1")
```

**Note.** The part lies in an exon of a single annotated transcript; ten others
splice over it. FLOT1 encodes flotillin-1, a lipid-raft protein. It lies in the
MHC, where LD spans megabases and many variants have GWAS hits, and it was
reported only after the clustering filter was dropped. We don't highlight it.

# Transcript-based isoLASER

None of the `r nrow(tb)` transcript-based genes carries a variant with a
brain-related Catalog entry. Of the `r sv("variants", "transcript_based")` variants
looked up, `r sv("variants_matched", "transcript_based")` have entries for other
traits only. HNRNPK's transcript-based variant is
rs296887, the one without a sleep entry.

# Trait classes

The grouping is ours. Each Catalog entry maps to one or more traits (EFO terms),
and each trait gets a class:

- **Neuropsychiatric disorder**: the Catalog's parent category is
  "`r rules[class == "neuropsychiatric disorder" & rule == "EFO parent term", terms]`"
  (the Catalog files psychiatric disorders there too). Or the trait name contains
  one of these: `r kw("neuropsychiatric disorder", "trait name contains")`.
- **Brain or behaviour**: the trait name contains one of these:
  `r kw("brain or behaviour", "trait name contains")`. A trait that also contains
  `r kw("brain or behaviour", "unless it also contains")` is excluded, so blood
  levels of brain proteins do not count.

Traits in neither class are not shown: blood counts, body size, metabolic
traits and so on. An entry whose traits fall in both classes counts as a
neuropsychiatric disorder.

Interaction and adjusted analyses also map their exposure as a trait. In "waist-hip
ratio × smoking" or "... adjusted for smoking", for example, smoking is mapped
next to the main trait. Those exposure traits are ignored unless the main trait is
itself one of them. The exposures are
`r kw("all classes", "exposure term dropped in interaction or adjusted analyses")`.

## Traits found in each class {.tabset}

Every trait with a genome-wide entry at our variants, with the genes, at
\|ΔPSI\| ≥ 0.05. **Catalog entries**: how many
Catalog entries with this trait match the listed genes' variants.

### Neuropsychiatric disorder

```{r traits_np}
trait_table("neuropsychiatric disorder")
```

### Brain or behaviour

```{r traits_bb}
trait_table("brain or behaviour")
```

# All brain-related hits {.tabset}

One row per gene × mapped trait (the Catalog's EFO terms for the entry), with
the Catalog's details:

- **Reported as**: the SNP the study reported. It differs from our rsID when
  dbSNP has since merged the two IDs. For FLOT1, the study reported rs115844366,
  now merged into rs3094125 at the same position.
- **Risk allele**: "not reported" when the study gave none.
- **p**, **OR or beta**, **Study** (first author and year), **Accession** (the Catalog study) and
  **PubMed**.
- **Entries**: how many Catalog entries with this trait match the gene's
  variant.
- **Class**: see [Trait classes](#trait-classes).

## Read-based isoLASER

```{r all_hits_read}
hits_dt(bh[version == "read_based"])
```

## Transcript-based isoLASER

None of the transcript-based variants has a brain-related Catalog entry.
